name: Space Shuttle Endeavour
best_known_for: OV-105 — fifth and youngest operational Shuttle, built to replace Challenger. Flew the first Hubble servicing mission STS-61 (1993), delivered ISS Node 1 Unity, Canadarm2, and Tranquility / Cupola
credit: Fifth and last operational orbiter, built from structural spares after the Challenger accident left NASA with only three flight-rated orbiters. Named via a national schools competition after Captain Cook's first vessel HMS Endeavour. First flight STS-49 (1992-05-07) included the first three-person EVA (to capture the stranded Intelsat VI satellite). Highlights: STS-61 (1993-12) — first Hubble servicing mission, restored Hubble's optics with COSTAR + WFPC2 replacement; STS-88 (1998-12-04) — first ISS assembly flight, delivered Node 1 Unity + the PMA mating adapters that connected to Russia's Zarya; STS-100 (2001-04) — installed Canadarm2; STS-118 (2007) — flew teacher Barbara Morgan, originally a Challenger backup; STS-130 (2010-02) — installed Tranquility + Cupola in one go; STS-134 (2011-05) — installed the AMS-02 cosmic-ray detector + final EVA crew of the Shuttle programme. On display at the California Science Center, Los Angeles, since 2012-10 (vertical stack with ET-94 + SRBs planned).

flights.flight_designation: STS-49 (1992-05-07) · first Endeavour flight; first 3-person EVA (Thuot + Hieb + Akers) — captured stranded Intelsat-VI by hand
STS-61 (1993-12-02) · first Hubble servicing mission (HST SM1); installed COSTAR corrective optics + WFPC2
STS-88 (1998-12-04) · first ISS assembly mission; delivered + attached Unity (Node 1) to Zarya
STS-100 (2001-04-19) · installed Canadarm2 robotic arm on ISS
STS-130 (2010-02-08) · installed Tranquility (Node 3) + Cupola on ISS — gave the station its iconic windows
STS-134 (2011-05-16) · final Endeavour flight; installed AMS-02 cosmic-ray detector on ISS
